Question: \(\triangle ABC\sim\triangle DEF\), and their areas are \(16\text{ cm}^2\) and \(36\text{ cm}^2\), respectively. The perimeters of the two triangles differ by \(10\text{ cm}\). Find the perimeter of the larger triangle, \(\triangle DEF\). (Unit: cm)
Solution: The area ratio is \(16:36\), so the similarity ratio is \(2:3\), and the perimeter ratio is also \(2:3\). Let the perimeter of \(\triangle ABC\) be \(2k\) and that of \(\triangle DEF\) be \(3k\). Then \(3k-2k=10\), so \(k=10\), and the perimeter of \(\triangle DEF\) is \(30\).
